newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up, Iraqi news lent bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up, Iraqi news lent bullish sentiment.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude futures were traded firmer on Monday amid strong sentiment on fresh Iraqi news and the resumption of trading of NYMEX futures on ACCESS, brokers said.
January Brent on SIMEX was traded at $22.85, higher from its last London's settlement of $22.77.

Brokers said the underlying firm sentiment caused by the resumption of trade on NYMEX after the Thankgiving break was given a further boost by news of Iraq sealing oil deals with foriegn firms under its oil-for-food deal.

Iraq foreign minister, Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf was quoted in Bagdad's state-run newspapers as saying that the oil ministry had begun signing contracts with international oil firms under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
The deal signed in May provides for limited oil exports of $2 billion every six months to enable Baghdad to buy food and medicine.
Brokers pegged resistance on the prompt month at $23 per barrel.
NYMEX January crude was last traded at $23.75 unchanged from its previous official settlement.
